mechanism_narrative: A lower current value of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, increasing equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of low-rate environments, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of high-unemployment instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of dual-decline instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 270.0 indicates persistent inflationary pressures that prompt Federal Reserve tightening, increasing risk-free rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of high-CPI instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of residential investment (RSAFS) indicates strong household spending on housing, supporting consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of high-residential-investment instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of high-unemployment instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals a liquidity trap where monetary policy is ineffective, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of liquidity-trap instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals manufacturing sector contraction that reduces corporate capital expenditure and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of industrial-contracting instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
